latest_release.name: CodeAssist 3.50.0
latest_release.body:
# 🚀 CodeAssist 3.50.0

**NEW: SWIFT ON YOUR PHONE** (install the **Swift** plugin from **Get plugins**)
- A real **Swift 6.4.3** compiler runs on the device: write a Swift program and **Run** it, with the standard library and Foundation.
- **Live SwiftUI previews** that look like an iPhone on iOS 26: lists and forms, navigation titles, the floating tab bar, toolbars, sheets, **Liquid Glass**, symbols and dark mode.
- Previews are **interactive**: tap buttons, toggles, pickers, links, tabs and sheets, with iPhone-style push, pop and sheet animations.
- **Run a SwiftUI app** (`@main struct MyApp: App`) full screen.
- **Code completion and errors as you type**, from Apple's own Swift language server.
- `@Observable` and other Swift macros work.
- Covers most of what iPhone apps use: `Picker`, `Menu`, grids, `DatePicker`, `TextEditor`, `Canvas`, custom view modifiers, gestures, materials and more.
- The plugin is large (about 190 MB) because it carries the whole Swift toolchain. One download per phone type (arm64, armv7, x86_64).

**KOTLIN**
- Fewer false errors: writes to smart-cast properties, Java interop types, `fun interface` receivers, and a `val` assigned in `init`.

**PREVIEWS**
- Fixed a crash when a layout preview frame was reused too early.

**PROJECT VIEW**
- A folder created outside the source folders now shows up.

**CHALLENGES**
- Runs count the work your code does, and a run with no results now says why.

**FOR PLUGIN AUTHORS**
- Plugins can index their own file types and query those indexes (plugin API 3.9.0).

Full changelog: https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases/tag/v3.50.0

# CodeAssist [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tyron12233/CodeAssist/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/actions) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tyron12233/CodeAssist?display_name=tag&sort=semver)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/tyron12233/CodeAssist)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2)](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW) CodeAssist is an IDE for Android that runs on Android. You can write Kotlin and Java, preview Compose and XML layouts, and build, sign and install APKs on the phone itself, without a computer or a remote build server. A desktop version for Windows and Linux is built from the same code.

## Features - Kotlin and Java editing: completion, auto-import, errors as you type with quick fixes, go to definition/implementation, reformat and optimize imports. - Android XML completion and validation for layouts, manifests and resource files. - Compose `@Preview` functions render next to the code and update as you edit. XML layouts preview too, including your own custom views. - Builds run on the device: aapt2, kotlinc, ecj, D8/R8 and apksigner. Builds are incremental. Output can be a debug APK, or a release APK or App Bundle signed with your own key. - Multi-module projects, build variants, ViewBinding, AIDL, KSP (Room, Hilt) and Firebase's `google-services.json`. - Dependencies from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, and local JAR and AAR files. - Import an existing Gradle project, or export a project as a Gradle project to open in Android Studio. - Git: clone, commit, branch, merge, stash and push. With a GitHub sign-in you can clone private repositories and open pull requests. - An optional AI coding agent that uses your own API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI or OpenRouter). - Plugins can add languages, build steps, tool windows and project templates. C/C++ (NDK) support is a separate plugin. ## Limitations - CodeAssist does not run Gradle. Build scripts are read when a project is imported (dependencies, version catalogs, the common `android {}` options), but Gradle plugins and custom build logic are not executed. - Only the bundled Kotlin compiler plugins are available: Compose, kotlinx.serialization and Parcelize. - Kotlin support is newer than Java support and has more rough edges. - Large projects are slow to index and build on phones with little RAM. If something you need is missing, open an issue. It helps to know what people are trying to build. ## Download - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases): the Android APK, and the desktop builds for Windows and Linux. - [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code) The Play build and the GitHub APK are signed with different keys, so one can't be installed over the other. ## How it works Gradle is too heavy to run on a phone, so CodeAssist keeps its own project model. Each module's build is a graph of tasks with up-to-date checks, much like Gradle's, and the tasks call the Android tools directly instead of going through the Android Gradle Plugin. Changing one file only re-runs the tasks that depend on it. Java analysis uses Eclipse JDT. Kotlin uses the Kotlin compiler's parser with CodeAssist's own analysis on top, so completion doesn't have to start a full compiler session on every keystroke. Symbol indexes for libraries and the Android SDK are stored on disk and read in place, which keeps memory use flat as projects grow. Compose previews don't install anything. The project's compiled code runs in a bytecode interpreter inside the IDE, against the real Compose runtime. More detail is in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), and the full list of documents is in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Building from source You need JDK 17 or newer (CI uses JDK 25). The Android SDK is only needed for the full build. ```sh # Core modules only: plain JVM, no Android SDK needed CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check # Everything, including the Compose UI and the Android app ./gradlew build # Run the desktop IDE ./gradlew :ide-desktop:run # Build the Android app ./gradlew :ide-android:assembleDebug ``` ## Project layout ``` platform/ core services with no IDE-specific knowledge; everything depends on it lang/ the language SPI, indexes, analysis, and the Java/Kotlin/XML backends build-system/ the incremental task engine and the JVM build pipelines run/ running project code on device: interpreter, bytecode VM, AWT/Swing android/ Android support: facets, variants, SDK data, layout preview services/ dependencies, version control, the project store, analytics, the AI agent plugins/ the plugin SPI and the host that loads plugins app/ the Compose UI and the Android, desktop and command-line launchers tools/ test harnesses ``` Gradle project paths are flat (`:lang-kotlin` lives in `lang/lang-kotlin`); `settings.gradle.kts` maps them. [docs/modules.md](docs/modules.md) describes each module. ## Tests and benchmarks Completion quality, editor latency, indexing and build performance are checked against committed baselines by the `regressionTest` tasks. The numbers below are regenerated on each release. | Area | Metric | Result | |---|---|---| | Java completion **quality** | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 75% / 0.88 | | Java completion **latency** (per keystroke) | member access / type ref | **4.3 ms** / 2.8 ms | | Symbol **index** quality | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 90% / 0.95 | | Symbol **index** query | prefix / fuzzy | ~4.4 µs / ~56 ns | Recall is how often the expected item appears in the completion list at all, top-1 how often it is first, and MRR the average of 1/rank. Latency is measured on the maintainer's machine, so treat it as a rough figure. **2614** tests passing across **441** suites · 0 failing · 4 skipped (framework / `CI_CORE_ONLY`). ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach. Before sending a pull request, run `CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check`; it is what CI runs. Plugin authors should start with [docs/writing-plugins.md](docs/writing-plugins.md). For questions and discussion, join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW). ## License CodeAssist is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The plugin SPI modules (`plugin-api`, `plugin-ui-api`, `platform-core`, `vfs-api`, `project-model-api`, `language-api`, `index-api`, `analysis-api` and `build-api`, published under `io.github.tyron12233`) also carry the Classpath exception (see [LICENSE-EXCEPTION](LICENSE-EXCEPTION)), so a plugin compiled against them can use any license. The license covers the code, not the name. A modified build needs its own name, icon and application id: see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).
